newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar stocks rise to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Qatar stocks rise to all-time high.

text.p: Solid gains by major shares at Qatar new stock market pushed up the index to an all-time high in the week to Thursday, brokers said.

"All in all, the high demand for shares has started to impact the prices and the outlook seems very favourable," Mazin al-Shakarchi, assistant general manager of treasury and investments at the Commercial Bank of Qatar, told Reuters.

The CBQ's 17-share index rose more than two points - the largest in recent months - to 133.91 points from 131.76 the previous week. The exchange, which launched formal operations on May 27, has not set up its own official index yet.
A total of 13,952 shares changed hands for 6.2 million riyals ($1.7 million) from 749,421 ($205,884) the previous week, the Doha Securities Market (DSM) said.
Services led with 7,528 shares changing hands for 3.75 million riyals, followed by banking with 6,224 shares for 2.45 million riyals.
Nine shares rose, three shed and five were unchanged.
Market leader, Qatar National Bank, advanced eight riyals to 563, CBQ rose five riyals to 315 and Qatar Islamic Bank climbed seven riyals to 144.
Qatar General Insurance clawed back 30 riyals to 450 after losing 270 riyal as it went ex-dividend two weeks ago. Last week it regained 45 riyal.

Other gainers included Qatar Insurance, which rose eight riyals to 560, Qatar Navigation which picked up 25 riyals to 750, Qatar Industrial Manufacturing, which gained six riyals to 68 and Qatar Real Estate, which climbed three riyals to 57. Qatar Shipping rose a riyal and a half to 47.50.
Losers included Al Ahli Bank of Qatar, which fell 20 riyals to 240 as it went ex-dividend, Qatar Cement, which shed two riyals to 305, and Qatar Flour Mills, which slipped one riyal to 305.
